title: Word detective: follow the clues

lessons.objective: Use a sentence to tell two sound-alike words apart.
Find out why dust can mean adding something or taking it away.
Test a possible link against every clue in a word puzzle.
Rearrange a word without adding, losing or duplicating a letter.
Spot a palindrome and distinguish its rule from an anagram.
Find the source words inside a blend and tell it apart from an anagram or a compound.
Check whether a sentence contains all 26 English letters and explain why repeats are allowed.

sources.name: Merriam-Webster — Open, closed and hyphenated compounds

glossary.definition: The words and situation around a clue that help you understand it.
Words that share a pronunciation but have different meanings.
A word with meanings that can be opposites.
A rearrangement of all the letters in a word or phrase to make another word or phrase.
A word or phrase whose letters read the same forwards and backwards, under the stated spacing and punctuation rules.
A word formed by blending parts and meanings of two or more source words.
A sentence or phrase containing every letter of an alphabet at least once.

outcomes: Use context to choose between homophones.
Recognise opposing meanings in familiar phrases.
Explain a connection that fits every clue.
Check that an anagram uses every original letter exactly once.
Test words and phrases for palindromes using a clear rule.
Recognise everyday portmanteau words and identify their ingredients.
Check a sentence for all 26 English letters and recognise that letters may repeat.
description: Seven short English lessons: follow sentence clues, explore meanings, shuffle letters, unpack word blends and find a whole alphabet. Optional quizzes included.
introduction:
A flower belongs in a vase. Flour belongs in a cake. They sound alike, so how do you know which one someone means?

Start with the clues around a word. Explore sound-alikes, meet words with opposite meanings and test a link across a set of clues. Then shuffle the letters of LISTEN into SILENT and find out what is hiding inside LEVEL. Unpack the two meals in brunch, then discover why a fox and a sleepy dog keep appearing in type samples.

Each lesson builds on the last. Read at your own pace, try the examples and take an optional short quiz when you feel ready. There is no timer.
prerequisites: You only need to read short English sentences. We explain each new term as it appears.
